items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: And Robinson and I stayed there until the police closed down.

ctx.x: And I wondered if that was before. No, I think that was after they left the Astoria. Mm-hmm.

They would often come down there with me, out to La Vida. Well, I think John, uh, Lee Collins and John Marrero left for, uh, left, uh, a tenor player there. Yeah, they went to Chicago and left him there. And they went to Chicago and left him there. And David Jones stayed there with me a long time. As a matter of fact, he opened up, uh, a teacher school uptown here somewhere. here some way. Alfred Williams stayed there a long time. Jim Robinson stayed there a long time. But uh, Alfred left and went to Texas. And…
Is that the sort of Mexican looking fella? Yeah, yeah, that's him. I think Andy Anderson was talking about that.

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1961-07-13
items.q: I worked with Handy at the Vida before I took the band in charge.

ctx.x: Let's see, we talked about recording too. That's another thing. Oh, oh Handy, we never did finish Handy. We better finish with it.

Where did you work with Handy? I worked with Handy. I worked with Handy at the Vida before I took the band in charge. I worked with Handy at the Vida. And after fired Handy, well they put me into the band, you see. They put me into the band, that's where I got Paul Bones and I got Kid Howard. Well they had, Shelly was playing trumpet then too. Shelly? Shelly, well they fired, the old man fired both of them fellas and he got handy in uh, in Kid Howard, old man's bikes.
Is that the Shelly that used to be with Paul Bones' Big Bam and in the, around Lake Charles, you know?
Jim Robinson on trombone. None of that.
Yeah, we got it, right? Now, when did you leave the La Vida? What year? Do you remember that?
